item.title: Beyond market size, European firms tap China's growth, innovation potential
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
SHANGHAI, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- Amid dazzling displays at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), a truck-sized turn-mill machine stands quietly, its computer-controlled spindle whirring.
Without flashy decorations, the machine still draws curious crowds. The attraction is a piece of precision machinery from an Austrian "hidden champion" WFL, shown under the expo's "deep-tech" label.
Weighing over 20 tonnes, the machine began its journey in August, crossing oceans and moving between trucks and shipping containers before arriving at the Port of Shanghai, host city of the CIIE -- a major platform for China to open its vast market to the world.
Why go to such lengths? Mayr Günther Franz Josef, general manager of WFL, told Xinhua that participating in the CIIE offers a chance to gain firsthand insights into China's rapidly upgrading high-end manufacturing sector and to forge closer ties with industrial partners across the Asia-Pacific region.
The company had another goal in mind: to make the machine's journey a one-way trip. As hoped, it found a buyer just three days into the expo.
Across the exhibition floor, European companies are deepening their engagement with China, drawn not only by the sheer size of its market but increasingly by opportunities arising from industrial upgrading, evolving consumer demand and a vibrant innovation ecosystem.
MORE THAN A VAST MARKET
China's pursuit of high-quality development, coupled with rising living standards, has fueled increasingly sophisticated demand for industrial and consumer products, opening up new avenues of growth for businesses worldwide.
"As China's manufacturing capabilities continue to advance, demand for high-end machine tools and other sophisticated industrial equipment is growing," said Zheng Xiaoli, a representative at WFL's booth. The company's machine tools are used to manufacture complex, high-precision components for industries including aviation, aerospace and shipbuilding.
The changing composition of their Chinese clientele offers a glimpse into that transformation. "Our customers in China used to be mainly state-owned enterprises and foreign-invested companies. Now, a growing number of private Chinese manufacturers seeking quality products are investing in our high-end machinery," said Zheng.
China's accelerating green transition and digital transformation are also creating fresh opportunities for European suppliers of advanced technologies and specialized materials.
For AMORNEX, a joint venture between Luxembourg-based steelmaker ArcelorMittal and China Oriental Group, the booming electric vehicle industry in China is driving demand for advanced materials.
Jurgen Cobbaut, the company's chief marketing officer, told Xinhua that some high-performance electric motors in Chinese EVs require materials with exceptional strength and efficiency, which plays to the company's strengths.
"It's not only the volume, but also the level of sophistication. That is what really makes it interesting," Cobbaut said of the Chinese market.
The shift toward more sophisticated demand extends to consumer markets, where changing lifestyles and rising expectations are also inspiring product innovation.
German cleaning equipment manufacturer Kärcher, for example, developed a compact, foldable pressure washer for cleaning bicycles, cars and camping gear, tapping into Chinese consumers' growing enthusiasm for outdoor activities. Originally designed for the Chinese market, the product has since been rolled out globally.
"Chinese consumers today are much more sophisticated. They're looking for products that fit their lifestyles," said Bernd Rützler, an executive vice president of Alfred Kärcher GmbH & Co. KG.
INNOVATION ENGINE
Beyond evolving demand, China's innovation capabilities, underpinned by its extensive supply chains and fast-evolving market, are becoming powerful draws for European companies.
"China has always been one of our most important strategic markets globally. What has changed is the increasingly multifaceted role China plays," said Liu Ling, chief region leader of Philips China.
For the Dutch health technology company, China is not only its second-largest market worldwide but also a "key supply-chain hub and engine of innovation."
Increasingly, innovations developed in China are also finding their way into European companies' global product portfolios.
Drawing on China's "strong industrial foundation, abundant innovation resources and diverse use cases," Schneider Electric has worked with Chinese partners to develop a range of proven, scalable solutions that are helping businesses across sectors become smarter, more efficient and greener, said Yin Zheng, executive vice president of China & East Asia Operations of Schneider Electric.
In the medical equipment hall at the CIIE, widely regarded as one of the expo's most competitive sections, Swedish medical equipment manufacturer Elekta is showcasing its AI-powered AutoART adaptive radiotherapy solution. The system can shorten the adaptive radiotherapy process -- from imaging and treatment planning to treatment delivery -- to just 10 to 15 minutes.
Developed in response to the demands of China's busy radiotherapy departments, this technology is intended for wider international use, according to Jin Jianxue, vice president and medical affairs director of Elekta China.
COMPLEMENTARY STRENGTHS
The CIIE offers a timely view of deepening business ties between China and Europe, as EU policymakers weigh trade issues with China.
The deeper ties are rooted in strong complementarity between the two sides, said Shen Yi, an international relations scholar at Fudan University. As China seeks to upgrade its industries and improve living standards, it needs European products and expertise in areas such as advanced equipment, precision instruments, pharmaceuticals and professional services, Shen told Xinhua.
Europe, in turn, stands to benefit from China's vast market, manufacturing capabilities and technological advances in sectors like batteries and solar power, he added.
Illustrating such complementarity, Zhang Shuo, chief representative at the Beijing Representative Office of the Brussels-based European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA), noted that Europe's century-old automotive industry has deep expertise in engineering, safety and environmental technologies, while China has taken the lead in batteries and electric mobility.
Cooperation is also moving beyond the traditional model of importing finished vehicles or transferring technology toward closer integration of industrial supply chains and joint research and development, he told Xinhua at their booth. ACEA is attending this year's CIIE as an exhibitor for the first time, although its member companies have long been regular participants.
Going forward, China has called for an "upward balance" in trade, achieved through greater openness and an expanding economic pie, rather than a "downward balance" caused by closing markets.
Ultimately, openness remains a powerful draw. As Rützler put it: "We see China as a reliable market and a reliable partner. Its continued opening up gives us the confidence to invest more."

item.title: Can Eisenkot form Israeli gov't after getting mandate?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
Gadi Eisenkot (C), former Israeli military chief and leader of the centrist Yashar party, delivers a speech at the centrist Yashar party campaign headquarters in Tel Aviv, Israel, Oct. 28, 2026. (Photo by Gil Cohen Magen/Xinhua)
JERUSALEM, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot received a presidential mandate on Sunday to form a government, giving him the first opportunity to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, after an October election stripped his right-wing coalition of a parliamentary majority.
But while Eisenkot has the backing of most lawmakers, deep divisions among Netanyahu's opponents leave him without a clear path to form a government.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (R) casts his ballot at a polling station in Jerusalem on Oct. 27, 2026. (Israel's Government Press Office/Handout via Xinhua)
WHAT DOES THE PRESIDENTIAL MANDATE MEAN?
On Sunday afternoon, President Isaac Herzog formally tasked Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, with forming a government at a ceremony in Jerusalem.
The decision follows consultations with parliamentary factions, during which 67 lawmakers recommended Eisenkot, compared with 46 who backed Netanyahu. Seven others declined to recommend either.
Under Israeli law, Eisenkot will have 28 days to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension granted by the president.
If he fails, Herzog could give another lawmaker, potentially Netanyahu, the opportunity to try. Such a scenario is not unprecedented. In 2021, Netanyahu failed to form a government and the mandate passed to Yair Lapid, who succeeded in forming a coalition. In 2019, both Netanyahu and his rival Benny Gantz failed to form a government, sending Israel to another election.
Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is sworn in.
Voters wait to cast their ballots at a polling station in Tel Aviv, Israel, on Oct. 27, 2026. (JINI via Xinhua)
CAN EISENKOT FORM A GOVERNMENT?
Israel's electoral system rarely gives a single party enough seats to govern alone, making coalition negotiations routine.
The 2026 election follows years of political turmoil, the devastating war in Gaza and mass protests against Netanyahu over his government's failure to prevent the Hamas-led attack on Oct. 7, 2023, and the handling of the wars that followed.
Eisenkot, a former army chief who entered politics in 2022, has emerged as a challenger appealing particularly to secular and liberal Israelis.
The Oct. 27 election gave Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc 53 seats in the 120-member parliament, down from 68, while opposition parties won 67. Yet Eisenkot's four-party alliance holds only 48 seats. The remaining 19 belong to two predominantly Arab parties.
Eisenkot could form a minority government if it wins a parliamentary vote of confidence, which requires more votes in favour than against, rather than an absolute majority of 61 lawmakers.
Eisenkot said he wants to swear in a national emergency government "as quickly as possible," initially comprising his alliance of right-wing, centrist and left-wing parties, with others joining later if they accept its principles.
In a statement on Friday on the social media platform X, he warned against Netanyahu's "dangerous entrenchment" in office and called for "stable and responsible leadership" to prevent another election.
Analysts say such a minority government plan would depend on support or abstentions from Arab lawmakers to survive a parliamentary confidence vote.
However, disagreements have emerged within Eisenkot's alliance over whether to seek support from Arab lawmakers in this vote of confidence.
Avigdor Lieberman, leader of the secular nationalist Yisrael Beytenu party, is pushing for a coalition of at least 61 lawmakers that would include ultra-Orthodox parties but exclude Arab parties.
He has urged a compromise over military conscription to bring the ultra-Orthodox into government, despite Eisenkot's election pledge to end longstanding exemptions from military service for ultra-Orthodox men.
Protesters call for unity and the formation of a new government through cooperation between Jewish and Arab parties at Habima Square in Tel Aviv, Israel, Nov. 7, 2026. (Photo by Jamal Awad/Xinhua)
Meanwhile, the Arab-led party Ra'am is seeking a more direct role in the next government.
Its leader, Mansour Abbas, told Israeli daily Haaretz that his party was holding talks with Eisenkot's bloc, including Eisenkot, about possible cooperation.
A senior Ra'am official told the newspaper the party's eight lawmakers would support an Eisenkot government in a confidence vote even without a coalition agreement.
The 11-seat Joint List has also offered to help remove Netanyahu, though neither Arab-led party has entered formal coalition negotiations with Eisenkot. Both have pledged to support replacing the parliament's speaker Amir Ohana, a Likud member.
Eisenkot and several allies have previously ruled out including Arab parties in their coalition, while Lieberman opposes a government dependent on their parliamentary support.
Netanyahu, meanwhile, has intensified his attacks on the prospect of Arab involvement.
In a video statement on Saturday, he accused Eisenkot of planning to govern with "terror supporters," warning that such a government would be too weak to confront threats from Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
"Israel simply will not survive with such a government," he said.
He instead called for a national unity government including all "Zionist parties," shifting from his campaign demand for a broad right-wing coalition.
Eisenkot has repeatedly ruled out serving under Netanyahu, although his party has left open the possibility of Likud joining a government under his leadership if it abandons its far-right allies.
The mandate gives Eisenkot a chance to end Netanyahu's rule, but his success depends on overcoming divisions over the very parties whose votes could bring him to power.

item.title: Trump says renewed strikes on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks progress
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
A child holds a placard during a rally against U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran outside the Los Angeles City Hall in California, the United States, March 7, 2026. (Photo by Qiu Chen/Xinhua)
WASHINGTON, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- U.S. President Donald Trump said Sunday that renewed military strikes on Iran were "highly unlikely" as long as negotiations made progress, but did not rule out further military actions.
In a phone interview with CNN, Trump claimed that the United States had already dealt a severe blow to Iran and that further military action was "highly unlikely" to be necessary.
"It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump noted, referring to Iran's nuclear program and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
The president also claimed that the United States had identified potential infrastructure targets in Iran, including power plants and bridges, and could destroy 38 bridges in an hour.
"Most likely it will not be necessary," Trump reiterated. "They want to make a deal so badly."
More than eight months after the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, Trump has repeatedly sent mixed signals about his willingness to end the conflict. Washington and Tehran remain at a stalemate, with little significant progress in diplomatic efforts.

item.title: APEC-year momentum fuels robust CIIE presence as Asia-Pacific economies tap China's open market
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
People visit the booth of Honda, a nine-year attendee of the China International Import Expo (CIIE), at the exhibition area of Automobile and Smart Mobility during the ninth CIIE in east China's Shanghai, Nov. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Lingyi)
SHANGHAI, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- As China hosts the 2026 APEC year, the ongoing ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) serves as a tangible demonstration of the Asia-Pacific pursuit of open regionalism, bringing together established multinationals, rising SMEs and industry innovators to turn China's enormous market potential into shared opportunities for the whole region.
Running from Nov. 5 to 10 in Shanghai, the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports has drawn wide-ranging delegations and exhibitors from across the Asia-Pacific. Southeast Asian players, including Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, alongside economies in Oceania and Northeast Asia, have brought consumer goods, advanced technologies and innovative services to the exhibition halls.
Paijit Viboontanasarn, vice chairman and secretary general of the Thai Chamber of Commerce in China, said in an interview with Xinhua that the CIIE offers Thai businesses a gateway to the Chinese market, helping smaller firms find customers and test business models while enabling larger companies to deepen cooperation.
"Beyond securing orders, the CIIE allows businesses to test whether their products and business models appeal to Chinese consumers," Paijit said. He described the expo in three words: "unique," "opportunity," and "openness," citing its import focus, opportunities for businesses of all sizes, and participation from across the world.
A staff member serves macadamia oil from Australia at the exhibition area of Food and Agricultural Products during the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai, east China, Nov. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Xiaoyu)
Thai brands are putting this into practice. Botanical fragrance maker Phutawan and snack producer MagMag are showcasing their signature products at this year's expo.
"Trade goes both ways," said Nonthakogh Panyapadhm, founder and CEO of MagMag. "Business can last only if both sides benefit."
Mark Lee, chairman of the Singapore Business Federation, noted that for Singapore businesses, the value of attending the CIIE "deepens over time."
"Many of our companies begin by using the CIIE to build visibility and gather market insights. Over several years, those initial engagements can grow into distribution agreements, joint ventures, and in some cases, regional partnerships that extend beyond China into Southeast Asia," Lee told Xinhua. The federation is leading a 54-company Singapore delegation for the ninth consecutive edition of the expo.
Samsung, the South Korean conglomerate, marks its ninth straight year at the CIIE. Zhang Daijun, senior vice president of Samsung China, pointed out that the group keeps expanding its high-end investment and local R&D footprint in China.
"China's firm commitment to expanding high-standard opening up has created more opportunities for international enterprises, and provided a stable and predictable environment for their development, injecting greater certainty into global trade cooperation," Zhang said.
People communicate at the exhibition area of Food and Agricultural Products during the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai, east China, Nov. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Haoming)
From the Southern Hemisphere, Australian and New Zealand enterprises are also actively engaging with Chinese consumers via the expo.
Rhys Roberts, national president and chair of the Australia China Business Council, said what matters most to Australian members is what happens after the expo. "Conversations that start on the show floor become distribution agreements, repeat orders and long-term partnerships, and that is where the real value lies," he said.
Sanchia Yonge, chief executive of New Zealand Trade and Enterprise, regards the CIIE as a valuable opportunity for New Zealand exporters to showcase products, understand the evolving Chinese market, strengthen brand awareness, and connect with customers and partners for long-term growth.
Blis Technologies, a New Zealand biotechnology company, is experiencing a new milestone this year, as it will have its own independent booth at the Shanghai expo. In just two years, sales of its oral probiotics products in China have exceeded 100,000 orders.
It's very important to attend the expo on a regular basis because the Chinese market is changing quickly, said Scott Johnson, CEO of Blis Technologies.
Humprey Arnaldo Russel, head of the ASEAN-China Research Center at the University of Indonesia, commented that the CIIE serves as a vital "gateway" for regional small and medium-sized enterprises to tap the Chinese market and build resilient trade networks amid shifting global dynamics.
"China gives opportunities to countries all across the globe," he said. "We need an open system where people with small and medium-sized enterprises, whether in Africa, Indonesia, Vanuatu, or Fiji, have the opportunity to trade across the globe based on WTO rules."

item.title: What to know about election of delegates to 21st CPC National Congress
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
BEIJING, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- The Communist Party of China (CPC), the world's largest governing party, has launched the process of electing delegates to its 21st national congress, which is scheduled to be held in the second half of 2027 in Beijing.
An official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee has explained why the election matters, how it will be organized, and what standards eligible candidates must meet. Here is what to know about the election.
The 21st CPC National Congress comes at a critical time when the CPC has been working to basically realize socialist modernization and heading toward the Second Centenary Goal. It will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country, as a new CPC Central Committee and a new CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection will be elected.
The 2,360 delegates to be elected should be outstanding Party members who carry the trust of more than 101 million CPC members and over 5.4 million Party organizations as they fulfill their duties at the congress.
The successful election of delegates and the completion of all tasks at the congress are vital to consolidating the Party's long-term governing position and enabling the Party to fully exercise its role as the leadership core. They are also closely linked to the prosperity and long-term stability of the Party and the country.
The election should be a process of studying and implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, particularly Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building.
Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has attached great importance to carrying out sound work related to the election. He heard multiple reports on this matter. He also presided over meetings of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, at which a circular on the election was deliberated and adopted.
The key to ensuring the success of the election is upholding the Party's overall leadership and the centralized, unified leadership of the CPC Central Committee.
Emphasis must be placed on examining candidates' political stance and awareness, as well as their capacity for political judgment, thinking and implementation. Their integrity and conduct must also be subject to strict scrutiny.
The delegates elected should be well-structured in composition and broadly representative, drawing from a wide range of fields, including the economy, science and technology, national defense, law enforcement and the justice system, education, public communication, culture, health, sports and social administration. They should also include workers in new forms of employment.
Front-line workers should account for an appropriate proportion of the delegates. Among delegates from provincial-level regions, central financial institutions and central state-owned enterprises in Beijing, Party members working on the front line should generally account for at least one-third. Among delegates from central Party and state departments, the proportion should generally be no less than 15 percent.
In regions where the new economy and new forms of business are thriving and there are large numbers of workers in new forms of employment, outstanding Party members from among these workers should also be recommended as candidates. Particular attention should be paid to recommending model workers, farmers and professionals as candidates. Women Party members and Party members from ethnic minority groups should each make up a certain proportion of the delegates.
Political, organizational and electoral disciplines must be strictly observed throughout the election process, with efforts made to prevent vote-buying and other electoral violations and strengthen oversight and enforcement.
The electoral procedure consists of five steps: nomination of candidates, assessment of nominees by electoral units, formation of a preliminary list of candidates, formation of a preparatory list of candidates, and formal election. The delegates will be elected through a process in which the number of candidates must exceed the number of seats by more than 15 percent. The delegates elected will be vetted by a qualification review committee prior to the national congress.

item.title: From products to partnerships, CIIE sets stage for global debuts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
People walk past an billboard themed on the ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE) at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) in east China's Shanghai, Nov. 5, 2026. (Xinhua/Xing Guangli)
SHANGHAI, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- For many global businesses, unveiling a new product or technology is more than showcasing innovation. It is also about reaching the right market.
Austrian machine tool maker WFL Millturn Technologies knows this well. To make its Asian debut, the company's massive new machining center crossed continents and oceans, traveling for more than two months before arriving in Shanghai for this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE).
"This visit to the CIIE will allow us to gain a close-up understanding of the development opportunities brought by the upgrading of China's high-end manufacturing industry," said Mayr Günther Franz Josef, WFL's general manager. A first-time participant at the expo, the company also hopes to deepen cooperation and strengthen ties with industrial partners across the Asia-Pacific region.
WFL's journey speaks to the CIIE's appeal as a proven platform for global businesses to launch debuts and connect markets, innovation and industries. Now in its ninth edition, this year's CIIE is seeing more than 480 exhibits making their global, Asian or China debuts.
The number sets a new record for the event, which has seen over 3,400 new products, technologies and services debut in the past eight editions. Many of them moved from the expo floor to store shelves and became bestsellers in the Chinese market.
For French cosmetics giant L'Oréal, the CIIE is an ideal launchpad for new brands, new products, new innovations, and new partnerships.
"Nearly half of our brands made their debut in the Chinese market through the CIIE," said Lan Zhenzhen, chief corporate affairs and engagement officer, L'Oréal North Asia & China. She added that these brands have since performed well in China.
In China's five-year development blueprint for 2026-2030, the country has called for expanding imports and continuing to hold the CIIE and other major trade fairs, as well as actively promoting the "debut economy."
"The Chinese market is a barometer for global product trends and innovation," said Xia Xianlin, account director at Joy Wing Mau Chile Spa. Introducing a new coconut product at the expo, the company hopes to leverage the CIIE's spillover effect to help more fruit products enter the Chinese market.
At the CIIE, debuts do more than introduce new products. They spark further innovation as technologies and ideas from around the world meet local needs and partners.
Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk, which has participated in all the previous eight editions of the expo, is showcasing new medicines at this year's event, including Kyinsu, a once-weekly injection for type 2 diabetes.
"The CIIE has become an important part of our work in China," said Mike Doustdar, president and CEO of Novo Nordisk. This is the company's ninth consecutive year at the CIIE, and many medicines first showcased at the expo have since reached the Chinese market.
According to Novo Nordisk, Chinese experts have helped develop Kyinsu, serving as lead investigators in its global Phase III clinical trial and helping shape the global research.
In telecommunications, U.S. tech company Qualcomm debuted the world's first 6G terminal prototype outside the laboratory. According to the company, the device has been used in 6G technology tests and validation conducted with its Chinese partners, including China Mobile and ZTE.
"Qualcomm's participation in the CIIE is more than a number of visits. It reflects our journey of innovating and growing together with our Chinese partners," said Frank Meng, chairman of Qualcomm China.
Unveiling a tire made with 75 percent renewable and recycled materials at the CIIE, French tire manufacturer Michelin has described its evolving approach to China as a shift from "In China, for China" to "With China, for the World."
New trends and technologies in sectors ranging from electric vehicles to autonomous driving often emerge in China ahead of other markets, according to Jay Wu, Michelin China vice president, director of government relations and strategy.
"China is both a test ground and a gym, a place where we test new ideas, challenge ourselves and continuously strengthen our innovation capabilities," Wu told Xinhua.

item.title: 7th World Media Summit opens in Beijing, highlighting media transformation in AI age
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
The 7th World Media Summit opens in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong)
BEIJING, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- The 7th World Media Summit held its opening ceremony in Beijing on Saturday under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action."
Xinhua News Agency and the Beijing municipal government jointly organized this year's summit, which runs from Thursday to Monday.
It drew nearly 500 representatives from nearly 330 mainstream media outlets, think tanks and government bodies from 112 countries and regions, as well as the United Nations and other international organizations.
Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony.
Yin Li, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee, also addressed the ceremony.
At the summit, delegates discussed the role of the media in the age of artificial intelligence (AI) and how the industry should respond to the challenges it poses. They called for closer cooperation to broaden access to advanced technologies and help media organizations worldwide develop together, while urging concrete steps to uphold journalistic ethics and safeguard the authenticity of news content as AI use expands.
Guests attend the opening ceremony of the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Chenlin)
INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT
Addressing the opening ceremony, Fu Hua, president of Xinhua News Agency, called on media professionals to share new technologies and applications, exchange experience in using them, and close gaps in AI research, development and understanding.
"We should lead the way in ensuring that all media professionals have a fair chance to benefit from AI," he said.
The 7th World Media Summit Beijing Consensus was adopted at the ceremony. It calls for joint efforts to advance the transformation and development of the global media industry in the AI era.
Recognizing AI's growing role in media development, the consensus commits to advancing the inclusive and responsible application of AI in the media sector so that advances in AI benefit media organizations at all stages of development and in every country.
AFP Chairman Fabrice Fries also stressed the need for inclusive AI development at the summit. "The benefits of this technological revolution should extend far beyond a small number of companies or countries," he said.
Fries called on media organizations, governments, businesses and universities to work together to ensure that AI helps build a healthier, more diverse global information ecosystem. In particular, AI models must be trained on datasets that reflect the diversity of human societies and perspectives, he said.
The World Media Summit was initiated in 2009 and is now a major global platform for media exchange and cooperation. The previous summit was held in 2024 in Urumqi, the capital city of northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.
For participants from Global South countries, the summit is particularly important in helping their media organizations adapt to the digital era and narrow development gaps.
Abdishakur Ali Ahmed, director of communication strategy at the Somalian Ministry of Information, Culture and Tourism, said the summit provides a platform for discussion about navigating digital transformation, which is central to Africa's development.
"The summit also offered us a chance to see China's digital transformation firsthand," he said, expressing hope that Somalia and other African countries would deepen cooperation with China to respond to shared challenges.
Luis Alves do Rosario Canhemba, senior director of the Information Office of Mozambique, said stronger international cooperation was essential for the country to facilitate its ongoing digital transformation.
He called for more exchanges on technology and joint efforts to address AI-related risks in the media industry, and expected expanded mutually beneficial cooperation between Mozambique and China as well as other Global South countries.
A guest experiences a pair of smart glasses ahead of the plenary session of the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 7, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong)
JOINTLY ADDRESSING RISKS
As AI is reshaping the entire chain of news production at an unprecedented speed, it has brought opportunities but also risks and challenges to the media industry, such as ethical lapses in the use of technology and the proliferation of false information, Lyu Yansong, editor-in-chief of Xinhua, said at the Summit on Saturday.
"We should take the initiative to share technological expertise, open-source models and training resources, and work together to strengthen our capacity to address risks arising from AI," he said.
On Saturday, the summit also released the Global Media Initiative for the Joint Development of AI Application Standards. Launched by Xinhua, the initiative brings together major media outlets and other professional organizations to safeguard the authenticity of information, protect data security, and uphold media ethics, thereby maintaining public trust in the media.
The first 22 participants also include Russia's TASS News Agency, the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), South Africa's Independent Media, and China's People's Daily and China Media Group.
Under the initiative, participants plan to work together for about two years to develop a set of standards that address different media uses of AI and are validated by media outlets. The initiative also calls for a global database of AI applications.
Dejan Jazvic, editor-in-chief of the Federal News Agency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, welcomed the summit's efforts to address AI-related challenges. "The standardization of AI applications must be established as soon as possible," he said.
"It is of crucial importance that we harness AI to improve and develop the media, rather than allowing it to serve as a replacement for media or as a tool for manipulating and deceiving the public," he said.
Mohammed Alyami, director general of the Union of News Agencies of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, said the theme of this year's summit, "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action," called on media organizations to build on shared commitments by proposing practical initiatives and forging partnerships.
He proposed an international framework for responsible journalism in the AI era, grounded in transparency, reliability and information verification.
Media organizations should ensure that technological change serves people and that the media always play a role as a bridge for mutual understanding and a platform for sharing the truth, he said.

item.title: Xi's reply inspires Australian students to carry forward friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
A student shows his panda doll award during the Panda Competition at the Chinese Embassy in Australia, in Canberra, Australia on Nov. 6, 2024. (Photo by Chu Chen/Xinhua)
ADELAIDE, Australia, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- As spring unfolds in the Southern Hemisphere, a message of friendship has crossed the ocean. Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to 110 young Australian students who had written to him, encouraging them to remain committed to promoting the China-Australia friendship.
In his letter dated Oct. 28, Xi said he was pleased to learn that the students recently visited China to take part in the Sino-Australian Collegiate Rowing and Dragon Boat Friendship Challenge, where they competed alongside Chinese university students, engaged in in-depth exchanges, forged friendships that transcended borders, and created wonderful memories together.
For many of the young Australians, the visit was more than a sporting and cultural exchange. It offered an opportunity to see China firsthand, connect with their Chinese peers and gain a deeper appreciation of the country.
Xi's reply has given their experience added significance, resonating with both the students and education professionals who helped make the exchange possible.
In July 2025, Xi met with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Beijing. Stressing the importance of cultivating people-to-people ties, Xi said Australians from all walks of life are welcome to visit the country and China stands ready to invite more Australian youth for exchange programs.
The invitation was taken up in September, when more than 100 students and staff members from six leading Australian universities, including the University of Sydney, Adelaide University and the University of New South Wales, visited China.
In China's eastern city of Nanjing, the young Australians joined students from Chinese universities, including Nanjing University and Tongji University, for the rowing and dragon boat event. Beyond the competition, the event also offered participants a chance to appreciate China's traditional dragon boat culture.
A contestant delivers a speech in the Australia Final of the 17th "Chinese Bridge" Chinese Proficiency Competition for Foreign Secondary School Students in Sydney, Australia, May 26, 2024. (Xinhua/Ma Ping)
The connections made during the trip did not end when the students returned home.
After their trip to China, the students jointly wrote a letter to Xi and Albanese, sharing their experiences during their visit, expressing admiration for China's long-lasting history and rich culture, as well as its scientific and technological innovation capabilities. They also voiced their eagerness to help carry forward the bilateral friendship and foster greater mutual understanding.
On Friday, Xi's reply was presented to representatives of the young Australians in Adelaide, South Australia's capital.
For Daniel Wiersema, a student representative from Adelaide University, receiving the letter was a particularly moving moment. Recalling the visit to China, he expressed gratitude to Xi for the opportunity and the experience.
"We want to thank him, and hope that our countries can become really, really good friends in the future," he said.
Jason Slater, head of Sport Development at Adelaide University Sport and Fitness, said he had spoken with students from all the participating Australian universities and found that they indeed enjoyed the trip.
The letter to the two leaders brought together the students' individual experiences and reflections, conveying personal stories and a strong sense of friendship, he said.
Xi's reply was "very important encouragement," Slater said. Many participants now hoped to return to China for further studies and explore opportunities to build connections with the country in their future careers, he said.
Members of an arts troupe from southwest China's Sichuan Province perform during a Chinese Culture Day event at Geelong College in Australia, Sept. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Xu Haijing)
Elise Courtney, a student at the University of New South Wales, recalled her excitement at receiving Xi's reply. "We know how busy it must be for him to take the time to reply to us. It was really special," she said.
She also showed Xinhua a team jersey she had swapped with a Chinese teammate, describing it as a treasured keepsake of the trip.
In their letter, the students recalled seeing China's dynamic, modern cities while also experiencing its rich history and cultural heritage. The contrast and combination left a strong impression on them.
Beyond the individual memories, the exchange also brought home a broader message about the role of young people in shaping bilateral relations.
China and Australia share a longstanding tradition of friendly exchanges, Xi noted in the letter, adding that the future of bilateral relations lies with the younger generation.
He voiced hope that the Australian students can continue to actively contribute to the cause of friendship between the two countries, serve as torchbearers of the friendship and cooperation between the two countries, and carry forward this friendship from generation to generation.
For Anja Felderhof, a student from Adelaide University, that message struck a particular chord. "That was my take-away sentence," she said.
"All of my friends in Australia can say we're pretty excited to continue this friendship as well," she added.
The importance of such exchanges extends beyond the students themselves, offering universities an opportunity to build lasting institutional links.
Rongyu Li, deputy vice-chancellor and vice-president (global engagement) of the University of Queensland, told Xinhua that face-to-face exchanges among young people from the two countries can deepen mutual understanding and foster friendship.
He said Xi's reply would encourage more Australian universities to actively participate in exchanges and further strengthen cooperation with China.
